nsclc_pt01_egfr_l858r_t790m_osimertinib_.title: Patient NSCLC-01: EGFR L858R/T790M Adenocarcinoma with Acquired C797S Osimertinib Resistance
nsclc_pt01_egfr_l858r_t790m_osimertinib_.citation: FLAURA / AURA3 Trials; Thress et al. (2015) Nature Medicine

clinical_history.primary_driver: EGFR L858R primary mutation + T790M gatekeeper, secondary acquired C797S mutation
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Rapid secondary progression at 4.1 months, diffuse bilateral pulmonary lymphangitic spread, death at 11.2 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: C797S mutation abolishes covalent binding of Osimertinib, maintaining uninterrupted downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling

nsclc_pt02_kras_g12c_sotorasib_resistant.title: Patient NSCLC-02: Poorly Differentiated Adenocarcinoma with KRAS G12C and STK11/KEAP1 Double Hit
nsclc_pt02_kras_g12c_sotorasib_resistant.citation: CodeBreaK 100; Skoulidis et al. (2018) Cancer Discovery; Negrao et al. (2023) JCO

clinical_history.primary_driver: KRAS G12C mutation, STK11/LKB1 biallelic loss, KEAP1 null mutation
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Primary resistance with disease progression at 2.6 months, multiple brain metastases, death at 6.8 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: STK11 loss hyperactivates mTORC1 while KEAP1 null stabilizes NRF2, driving high antioxidant flux and bypassing KRAS dependency

nsclc_pt03_alk_eml4_fusion_lorlatinib_re.title: Patient NSCLC-03: Signet-Ring Adenocarcinoma with EML4-ALK and Compound G1202R Solvent-Front Mutation
nsclc_pt03_alk_eml4_fusion_lorlatinib_re.citation: CROWN Trial; Shaw et al. (2019) JCO; Gainor et al. (2016) Cancer Discovery

clinical_history.primary_driver: EML4-ALK Variant 3 fusion + acquired solvent-front ALK G1202R mutation
clinical_history.hospital_treatment: Alectinib followed by Lorlatinib (3rd-generation brain-penetrant ALK TKI)
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and spinal drop metastases at 5.2 months, death at 13.5 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: G1202R mutation introduces steric clash with Lorlatinib, maintaining persistent STAT3 and PI3K/Akt pro-survival signals

nsclc_pt04_met_exon14_skipping_capmatini.title: Patient NSCLC-04: Pulmonary Sarcomatoid Carcinoma with MET Exon 14 Skipping and High Gene Amplification
nsclc_pt04_met_exon14_skipping_capmatini.citation: GEOMETRY mono-1; Wolf et al. (2020) NEJM; Paik et al. (2015) Cancer Discovery

clinical_history.primary_driver: MET Exon 14 skipping splice site mutation + high focal MET gene amplification (GCN >10)
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Initial short stability then fulminant pleural effusion and chest wall invasion at 3.3 months, death at 6.1 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: Secondary D1228N kinase domain mutation blocks Capmatinib, while high HGF autocrine flux hyperactivates STAT3 and MCL-1

nsclc_pt05_egfr_ex19del_acquired_met_byp.title: Patient NSCLC-05: Asian Non-Smoker EGFR ex19del with High-Level MET Amplification Bypass
nsclc_pt05_egfr_ex19del_acquired_met_byp.citation: FLAURA Trial; Soria et al. (2018) NEJM; Engelman et al. (2007) Science

clinical_history.primary_driver: EGFR exon 19 deletion with high focal c-MET amplification emerging under 1st-line Osimertinib
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Progression-free survival of 6.0 months, rapid bilobar liver metastases, death at 14.0 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: Emergence of MET amplification recruits ERBB3 and drives constitutive PI3K/Akt activation, bypassing EGFR inhibition

nsclc_pt06_pdl1_high_immunotherapy_excep.title: Patient NSCLC-06: Heavy Smoker Squamous Lung Cancer with PD-L1 95% Exceptional Responder
nsclc_pt06_pdl1_high_immunotherapy_excep.citation: KEYNOTE-024 / KEYNOTE-042; Reck et al. (2016) NEJM; Rizvi et al. (2015) Science

clinical_history.primary_driver: High Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB), PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) 95%, All-Wild-Type Drivers
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Complete pathological and metabolic response (CR), ongoing disease-free survival >54 months (SURVIVED / Cured)
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: Intact caspase and Bak/Bax machinery; absence of oncogene-driven Bcl-2/Mcl-1 locks permits complete immune eradication

nsclc_pt07_squamous_pi3k_akt_sox2_amplif.title: Patient NSCLC-07: Central Bronchogenic Squamous Carcinoma with PIK3CA Mutation and Severe Hypoxia
nsclc_pt07_squamous_pi3k_akt_sox2_amplif.citation: TCGA-LUSC Consortium; Hammerman et al. (2012) Nature; Perez-Ramirez et al. (2015)

clinical_history.primary_driver: PIK3CA E545K helical domain mutation, TP53 R248W mutation, high necrotic hypoxia signature
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Primary chemo-refractory disease, local cavitation, mediastinal invasion and death at 4.8 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: Constitutive PI3K/Akt signaling directly phosphorylates and inactivates BAD and Caspase-9, preventing chemotherapy-induced apoptosis

nsclc_pt08_pan_refractory_kras_tp53_keap.title: Patient NSCLC-08: Highly Aggressive Triplet-Mutant KRAS/TP53/KEAP1 Metastatic Lung Carcinoma
nsclc_pt08_pan_refractory_kras_tp53_keap.citation: Arbour et al. (2018) Clin Cancer Res; TCGA-LUAD; Ricciuti et al. (2022) JTO

clinical_history.primary_driver: Concurrent KRAS G12V, TP53 R273H, KEAP1 null mutation, strong TGF-beta mesenchymal stroma
clinical_history.real_world_outcome: Progression-free survival of 1.9 months, extensive hepatic and adrenal metastases, death at 4.9 months
clinical_history.known_resistance_mechanism: Co-occurring KRAS, p53, and KEAP1 defects hyper-stabilize NRF2, MCL-1, and XIAP, rendering both chemo and checkpoint blockade ineffective
